subject: LLM private-deploy connectivity options — FinTrek (VPC peering vs PrivateLink vs S2S VPN)
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
To: Alex Galloway <alex.galloway@fintrek.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 25 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: LLM private-deploy connectivity options — FinTrek (VPC peering vs PrivateLink vs S2S VPN)

Hi Alex—and Maya (looping in case you want to add constraints),

Thanks again for the time this morning. Per our conversation I put together a concise comparison of the three common connectivity patterns for Redwood Private (VPC/on‑prem) deployments so you can choose a path that meets FinTrek's compliance and latency needs. I'm attaching a simple diagram and a draft mutual action plan (MAP).

Top-level summary (short):
- VPC Peering: lowest operational overhead if both sides are in the same cloud account family; simple routing, good performance. Not suitable if FinTrek requires strict cross-account isolation or wants service endpoints with fine-grained access controls.
- AWS PrivateLink / Interface Endpoints: best isolation and least blast radius — Redwood exposes an interface endpoint in your VPC that connects to our private service endpoints. Good for strict auditability and easier to restrict traffic to a single service. Slightly more complex to set up and can have per-ENI costs.
- Site-to-Site VPN (IPsec): highly flexible for on‑prem and multi-cloud; easiest to approve from a compliance standpoint when customers insist on direct tunnels to their network. Latency and throughput depend on customer gateway and internet path; useful for hybrid architectures or short-term pilots.

Practical recommendation (initial):
1) If FinTrek requires dedicated service isolation and private endpoints for compliance, PrivateLink + restricted CIDR ranges is the recommended default.
2) If FinTrek cannot accept interface endpoints for policy reasons and both VPCs are in the same cloud tenancy, Peering is simplest.
3) If you have on‑prem or multi-cloud sites and strict on‑prem routing/inspection requirements, use S2S VPN as the ingestion layer; consider a PrivateLink front for production traffic once we validate performance.

Outstanding questions that affect a final choice:
- Will FinTrek allow cross-account VPC peering or is cross-account peering blocked by policy?
- Do you need HSM/KMS integration for request authentication at the customer boundary?
- SLOs: what's your 99th percentile latency SLO to the inference endpoint?
- Are audit logs required to show per-customer API calls in your KMS/Audit pipeline?

Next steps I propose: sketch a quick alpha architecture for PrivateLink + Transit (if you need hub-and-spoke), include KMS/HSM callouts, and draft a provisional SOW. If you prefer, we can run a short pilot over a VPN tunnel first to validate tokenized traffic and latency.

Attachments: redwood-network-diagram.pdf, fintrek-mutual-action-plan.xlsx

Thanks,
Dylan
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Alex Galloway <alex.galloway@fintrek.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 25 Jun 2027 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: LLM private-deploy connectivity options — FinTrek (VPC peering vs PrivateLink vs S2S VPN)

Dylan,

Appreciate the clear summary. A few constraints from our side that will drive the decision:
- Security policy: cross-account VPC peering is restricted by default (we need an exception with security and network approval).
- Compliance: we need FIPS-compliant endpoints for any KMS interactions and full auditability of who called what; the security team will insist on per-request logs being forwarded to our Splunk tenancy.
- Latency SLO: our product team needs p99 < 150ms for inference requests (post-auth) from our primary app region.
- On-prem fallback: we do have an on‑prem site in NYC that sometimes needs low-latency access; for that we prefer a VPN path.

So far this points us toward a PrivateLink fronted architecture with a VPN for the on‑prem fallback and a canary peering option if we get the peering exception. Can you include audit log forwarding details and KMS/HSM integration options in the SOW? Also, do you have any reference docs or SOC2 artifacts on how you provide per-request audit logs when using PrivateLink?

If you can send a revised MAP and a provisional SOW we can pull in security and procurement next week. Also, Maya from our security team copied here will be the primary for the questionnaire.

Thanks,
Alex
VP Product — FinTrek Labs
---
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 25 Jun 2027 12:07:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: LLM private-deploy connectivity options — FinTrek (VPC peering vs PrivateLink vs S2S VPN)

Kim / Ben — forwarding Alex's constraints from FinTrek. Key callouts: cross-account peering is blocked by policy (they'll request an exception), they require FIPS-level KMS/HSM interactions, per-request audit logs into their Splunk, and p99 latency target of 150ms. They also want a VPN for on‑prem NYC fallback.

My suggested approach (concise implementation plan):
- Primary: PrivateLink (interface endpoint) in the FinTrek VPC(s) pointing to Redwood's Private service endpoints. Rationale: meets isolation/auditability and limits lateral access; aligns with their compliance ask.
- Transit/hub: If FinTrek expects multi-VPC spines, propose AWS Transit Gateway owned by FinTrek to reduce per-peering management; attach interface endpoints and subnets for ENIs.
- KMS/HSM: Redwood supports customer-managed keys (CMKs) for encryption at rest and can integrate with an external HSM for key signing if required; we'll include the integration options in the SOW (note: FIPS endpoint compliance will require configuration and possibly dedicated hardware).
- Logs: We can stream per-request logs (redwood callIDs, timestamps, model id, route) to a secure S3 bucket or Kinesis and set up an encrypted forwarder to FinTrek's Splunk. We'll include a 90‑day raw retention (configurable) and a pipeline for per-request redaction rules.
- DR/fallback: Establish an S2S VPN from FinTrek on‑prem to a Redwood VPN concentrator for low-latency on‑prem traffic; failover rules in the MAP.
- Cost/ops tradeoffs: PrivateLink has per-ENI and data-processing costs; Transit Gateway adds fixed hourly and attachment fees. VPN has modest monthly cost but variable throughput/latency.

Action items for SOW draft:
1) Add KMS/HSM integration options and responsibilities (who holds keys vs who signs requests).
2) Define audit log delivery method, retention, and encryption.
3) Pilot plan: 2-week VPN pilot validating p99 latency from NYC site, followed by PrivateLink cutover for production with a canary rollout.
4) Implementation milestones and acceptance tests (latency, throughput, log delivery).

Can you review and flag any missing pieces? If agreed, I'll prepare a provisional SOW and include an architecture diagram showing the PrivateLink + Transit pattern with VPN fallback.

Thanks,
Dylan
(On behalf of Solutions)

Thanks Dylan — good synthesis. A couple of additions before we send the SOW draft to FinTrek's procurement/security:

- Include KMS key origin options: (a) Redwood-managed CMK with envelope encryption, (b) customer-managed AWS CMK in FinTrek account (preferred for control), (c) external HSM integration with attestation (if they insist on FIPS hardware). Spell out which controls each option supports.
- Log delivery: provide both push (Kinesis Firehose -> Splunk forwarder) and pull (S3 + signed URL) patterns; include encryption-at-rest and rotation notes.
- Network ACLs / CIDR hygiene: limit interface endpoint ENIs to a narrow CIDR block and call out exact ports for the inference API (443 + health ports) so FinTrek can scope their firewall rules.
- Acceptance tests: must include p99 latency measurement (FinTrek to Redwood) using their sample traffic generator; include an objective pass/fail threshold and a measurement window.

Once those are in the SOW we can send to Alex + Maya. Ben — can you price PrivateLink per-ENI + TGW attachment + VPN concentrator (monthly and estimated egress) so we can include a ballpark in the MAP?

If all good I'll prep the provisional SOW and schedule a short meeting next week with FinTrek security.

Kimberly Park
Head of Solutions — Redwood Inference
